>

> interpreted as "one".

Ian can play cards that require [cel] or [for], right?
But he can't play Forced March.

> Alia's "or" is not to be interpreted as a logical "or"?

No, it is to be interpreted as a grammatical or.

It is not to be interpreted as a superset of a logical "and".

> What about the new card (don't want to spoil card as a lot of people
> on this side yet have to play their pre-releases) that targets X
> vampires controlled by prey or predator? If X is two I can't target
> one vamp belonging to prey and one belonging to predator?

You can. It will then be undirected.

Each chosen minion is controlled by either your predator or
your prey. None of the chosen minions is controlled by both
your predator and your prey.

> When I have Barth ready and untapped, must I decide if his ability
> works on either prey or predator each time Barth becomes ready and
> untapped?

Similarly, no.
